text.p: Aiming to compete against Southwest Airlines, USAir Group is asking its pilots to go along with the idea of a low-cost airline-within-an-airline that would soak up as much as 40 percent of USAir's flying time, The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.
The Journal said that though negotiations are far from complete, the low-cost concept is crucial to the company's turnaround plans.

The newspaper cites a union briefing document that says pilots who fly for the proposed low-cost line, dubbed US2, would earn less than their colleagues on the "main line," fly more hours and receive less vacation and sick-leave.
The Journal said USAir declined to comment.
